nm_yucca_flower_tower.blurb: Yucca Flower Tower is a granite formation in Echo Canyon on the west side of the Sandia Mountains above Albuquerque, close to the La Luz Trail near the Sandia Crest. It is more a concentrated cluster of good lines than a true tower. Thirteen climbs are mostly traditional multi-pitch routes, with a few in the alpine style. Grades run widely, from easy fifth class up to the 5.14 range, but the bulk sit between 5.10 and 5.11, so it suits confident trad leaders. The usual way in is a rappel down from the ridge above, with double ropes for the lower sections, which makes it a committing day.

nm_upper_science_friction.blurb: Upper Science Friction is the higher of two walls in the Science Friction zone of Nova Canyon, on the west side of the Sandia Mountains near Albuquerque. Long, clean granite faces hold thirteen climbs, mainly trad with a handful of alpine-style lines plus one sport route and one aid line. Most grades fall between 5.8 and 5.11, with a few harder ones up to 5.12 and an easy 5.6 on the low end. Lines are cleaned and equipped with bolts and lowering anchors, though cracks on the left still want removable gear. The wall is in shade until mid-morning, then catches sun. Helmets are wise because rock quality varies.

nm_little_beaver_town.blurb: Little Beaver Town is a small granite crag on the east side of Albuquerque, tucked into an arroyo and partly hidden by trees. The wall faces north. Thirteen routes are mostly traditional, with several top-rope lines and one sport route, and the grades are friendly: a spread of 5.6 to 5.8 with a few 5.9 and 5.10 climbs. That makes it a handy spot for beginners, short outings and top-rope practice, since anchors can be set by walking around to the top. It is close to town and quick to visit, but small, so expect to exhaust it in a short session.

nm_el_norte.blurb: El Norte is a small bolted sector near the village of El Rito in northern New Mexico, on national forest land. The rock is cobble conglomerate, with the cobbles and the pockets they leave serving as holds. All thirteen routes are sport climbs, short at roughly 40 to 60 feet. Grades run from 5.9 to 5.12, mostly in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, so it suits climbers warming up on moderates as well as those pushing into the low 5.12s. A cleaned lower slab holds a few routes, and a wooded grotto above it is still undeveloped and not recommended for now.

nm_love_shack_area.blurb: The Love Shack is a short, steep sport wall in the Las Conchas area of the Jemez Mountains, set in a bend of the East Fork river with some lines running out over the water. Thirteen sport routes range from 5.9 to 5.13, but the weight is on 5.12, which suits climbers looking for steep, bouldery pumpy climbing on rhyolite. A few moderates in the 5.9 and 5.10 range offer an easier way in. The overhang keeps the routes dry in rain, though a rising river can complicate the base, and stick-clipping the first bolt is advised.

nm_back_rocks_the.blurb: The Back Rocks is a quiet rhyolite crag in upper Rendija Canyon, northwest of Los Alamos, reached by hiking the Mitchell Trail past Clifty and Thanksgiving Rock. Thirteen routes mix sport and trad, with grades from 5.6 up to 5.12 and most falling around 5.9 to 5.11. The walk in is longer than at neighbouring crags and finishes with a bushwhack and scramble to the base. The wall catches sun most of the day, and fire damage has thinned the surrounding trees. It is rarely visited and quality is mixed, so it suits locals wanting solitude more than a destination trip.

nm_frontera.blurb: Frontera is a trad wall in the Organ Mountains east of Las Cruces, on the lower flank of the range below the Needle and Squaretops. Thirteen routes are mostly traditional, many of them multi-pitch cracks and dihedrals, plus a couple of aid lines and a top-rope. Grades span easy fifth class to 5.12, with the majority between 5.8 and 5.10. The face points southeast, so it takes good winter sun but can be hot in summer, though some lines are shaded by afternoon. The walk in is long and steep, and with little climbing history on record, loose rock is possible.
